classification.interventionType: agentic blog drafting and PR creation

decisions.selected: Recovered adoption intent from the workflow's first commit (15bc81bcf06ee72df0508c7f72e90ed26d943691, PR #31981, merged 2026-05-13T16:50:09Z): the workflow must draft one Agent-of-the-Day blog entry per weekday and finish by calling create_pull_request, with a 7-day expiry safe-output.
alternatives: Treating blog-entry drafting/content quality itself as the outcome
decisions.rationale: The adoption commit's safe-outputs.create-pull-request block (with expires: 7d) and the current version's mandatory-completion rule (create_pull_request/noop/report_incomplete) are the only adoption-time signals of what counts as done; content quality is not adjudicable without agent judgment.

decisions.selected: One blog-publication opportunity per UTC calendar date the run started (the weekday blog slot), independent of which workflow the agent chose to spotlight.
alternatives: One opportunity per spotlighted workflow name
One opportunity per run id with no shared key
decisions.rationale: The workflow is scheduled daily on weekdays and skip-if-match prevents concurrent duplicate PRs for the same slot; the spotlighted workflow is an agent choice each run and cannot be recovered deterministically for historical runs, so the calendar date is the only assignment stable enough for reruns to share a key.

decisions.selected: opportunityKey = blog-day:<UTC date of run.createdAt>, derived by a pure date computation from the run subject so it never requires GitHub API access.
alternatives: opportunityKey = run:<run id> with no clustering of same-day reruns
decisions.rationale: Duplicate reruns or manual dispatches for the same weekday must repeat the same key so downstream analysis can cluster them, per the design procedure's overlapping-ownership guidance.

decisions.selected: Accepted evidence is a merged github/gh-aw pull request whose body contains this workflow's gh-aw-tracker-id marker and the exact numeric run id (from the gh-aw-agentic-workflow footer 'id: <runId>,' field), found via GitHub Search REST (search/issues).
alternatives: Matching by PR title date text (titles are inconsistently formatted across history: '[blog] ...', 'blog: ...', 'Agent of the Day – ...')
Matching by added file path under docs/src/content/docs/blog/ (path/date format also varies and duplicate-suffix files complicate exact matching)
decisions.rationale: The gh-aw footer marker with the numeric run id is emitted by the platform (generate_footer.cjs) on every safe-output PR since adoption and uniquely ties a specific run to its resulting PR, unlike free-form titles or paths that changed format multiple times across the workflow's history.

decisions.selected: Seven days (604800 seconds) after run.createdAt, matching the workflow's create-pull-request expires: 7d safe-output configuration.
alternatives: No maturation window (grade only at evidenceAt)
30-day window matching generic PR review SLAs
decisions.rationale: The safe-output itself declares the PR expires after 7 days if unmerged, so 7 days is the frozen, contract-derived point past which an unmerged PR is no longer expected to be merged as the same opportunity; the adoption run's own PR (#31981) merged the same day it was opened, well inside this window.

decisions.selected: Binary primary metric: 1 when a merged pull request tagged with the run's id exists by evidenceCutoff, otherwise 0; null when the request is invalid or pull-request search evidence is unavailable.
alternatives: Proportion metric based on blog post word count/SEO-metadata compliance (an output-quality proxy, not attainment)
Counting PR creation (not merge) as attainment
decisions.rationale: The workflow's operational purpose is a published blog post, and only a merged PR is accepted repository evidence of publication; PR creation alone is an activity signal that a human reviewer could still reject, and word-count/SEO checks are output-quality proxies explicitly excluded from primary attainment.

alternatives: baseline-comparable using the pre-adoption weekly blog cadence's merge rate
decisions.rationale: Pre-adoption blog posts were hand-authored on an irregular weekly/monthly cadence with no per-run subject or tracker-id marker to score with the same run-scoped metric, so no comparable frozen pre-adoption evidence exists under this contract.
evidenceReferences: git log docs/src/content/docs/blog/ (pre-2026-05-13 posts: manual weekly-update PRs, no gh-aw tracker-id marker)

decisions.selected: merge-latency-health diagnostic: clamp(1 - (mergedAt-createdAt)/604800, 0, 1) reported only when merged by evidenceCutoff, aggregated as a mean and kept separate from the primary value.
alternatives: Word-count or SEO-metadata-length compliance as a diagnostic
decisions.rationale: Merge latency relative to the workflow's own 7-day expiry window gives normalized context on how promptly published entries clear review without being combined into the binary primary attainment value.

uncertainties.description: GitHub Search REST (search/issues) results are capped at 100 items per query without pagination; if far more than 100 merged blog PRs carrying this tracker-id accumulate, the oldest matches could fall outside the search window used by a single query.

Search indexing latency on GitHub could delay a just-merged PR from appearing in search results for a short period, which could transiently score a just-attained opportunity as 0 until the index catches up.
Because the design is attainment-only, there is no quantitative reference point for whether daily automated publication represents an improvement over the prior manual weekly cadence.

A legitimate noop (when the agent finds no trustworthy live evidence after checking multiple workflows) is indistinguishable from a failed attempt under this contract; both score 0 for that day's opportunity, since accepting agent judgment about noop legitimacy is explicitly disallowed.
